description: Beyond space, beyond time, beyond the known. We are Yog-Sothoth — a team of curious minds exploring the unknown, turning cosmic mysteries into innovative solutions through science, technology, and creativity. The universe is our playground; discovery is our mission.
summary: RedShift helps smallholder farmers make more informed planting decisions as weather becomes less predictable. It turns NASA Earth observations—including long-term NASA POWER climate records, GPM/IMERG precipitation, MODIS vegetation data and SRTM terrain—into a clearer picture of conditions around a field. By comparing recent conditions with historical patterns, RedShift highlights potential rainfall and crop stress, then presents crop-rotation options with plain-language explanations of the factors behind them. The first demonstration focuses on Kerala’s crops and local farming context, but the approach is designed to adapt to other regions using globally available Earth-observation data and locally relevant information. Recommendations are transparent and support, rather than replace, farmers’ knowledge and judgment. RedShift’s goal is to make satellite data useful at the field level, helping farmers spot changing conditions earlier and plan their next season with greater confidence.
details:
RedShift is a field-level decision-support tool for farmers facing increasingly unpredictable seasons. A farmer marks a field on the map, and the system builds a profile using NASA Earth observations and soil data. It compares recent weekly conditions with long-term climate patterns to identify sustained rainfall deficits, unusual heat and vegetation changes. Missing observations are shown as gaps rather than treated as normal conditions.

The analysis then combines field conditions with crop requirements, planting windows and the farmer’s season history to compare crop-rotation options. Farmers can adjust rainfall and temperature assumptions to see how the recommendations change under drier or hotter conditions. Each option shows the main risks and the factors behind its score, so the farmer can make the final decision with local knowledge.

The first version is focused on Kerala, where the crop calendar and farming context shape the recommendations. The same approach can be adapted elsewhere by adding local crops and planting information to globally available Earth-observation data. The project uses NASA POWER climate records, with GPM/IMERG rainfall, MODIS vegetation observations and SRTM terrain data where available. It is built with Python and FastAPI, Next.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL, and is designed to work through a regular phone or computer browser without specialized hardware.
